newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk army says Islamist children take militant vow.
newsitem.headline: Turk army says Islamist children take militant vow.

text.p: Turkey's military has shown politicians the text of what it says is a militant Islamist vow recited by children being taught to overthrow the secularist system, newspapers said on Wednesday.
"I swear by Allah...to strive to create a state based on religion and Islamic law in Turkey and to devote myself to the war against Mustafa Kemal atheism," the Sabah daily quoted the vow as saying.
The Milliyet newspaper printed the same text.

The papers said the vow, alleged to be recited at underground Koran classes for children, was presented at a meeting of the military-dominated National Security Council last week as evidence of a dangerous Islamist upsurge.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan also attended the meeting, which produced a warning to the government to clamp down on what the military views as Islamist extremism.

The army sees itself as the guarantor of Turkey's official secularism, established by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk who founded modern Turkey as a republic in 1923. Ataturk was originally a military commander.

Milliyet said the security council was shown a video of young Koranic students spitting at a statue of Ataturk, a widely revered figure. The council meeting was closed to the press but its minutes have been leaked to the press.
Sabah said 160,000 Turkish children study Islam at illegal Koran courses. Bringing the classes under the control of the Education Ministry is one of a list of anti-Islamist demands made by generals.
Erbakan, NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader, has so far refused to heed the army's orders.
